change: Smart-factor backend fixed: gtsam's Python wrapper binds setLandmarkDistanceThreshold/setDynamicOutlierRejectionThreshold as bool, so 40.0 -> True -> 1 m and every landmark beyond 1 m was FAR_POINT (error 0, IMU-only drift). Disabled both (False) and gate in podslam instead. Synthetic 29.2 -> 1.10 cm; 0 resets and 0 failed solves in every condition (explicit backend: 17.4/22.1/29.6 with 10-39 rebuilds). RPE p95 6.6 cm vs cuVSLAM 21.6.

change: Proper marginalisation + chi2 gate + IMU noise inflation. (1) Sliding-window prior is a real Schur complement (LinearContainerFactor) instead of the over-confident full-window marginal pin: exact on synthetic (0.35 cm) once the first pose is hard-anchored (gauge random-walk otherwise) and LM stops on absolute error (the prior's constant term defeated the relative test). (2) chi2 gate on the converged whitened reprojection error (5 per measurement) retires outlier landmarks and keeps them out of the prior. (3) Estimator-side IMU noise inflation (Basalt's TUM-VI values 5.7/1.8/1.2/4.5): with datasheet values the 200 Hz IMU pinned every keyframe translation to 0.1 mm and dictated a -1.3 % scale; now scale 0.99-1.00, yaw drift 2.9 -> 0.9 deg/min. 0 resets, 0 failed solves (cuVSLAM 11.4/13.1/17.2, Basalt 10.8/28.5/20.9, OpenVINS 7.4/7.6/6.1). EPI (nonlinear landmark refinement) unusable: gtsam throws CheiralityException inside LM.
next: Night gap (17.4 vs 8.8 day): 1734 vs 935 outlier landmarks and 300-track saturation on noise -> feature quality gate tied to the image noise level, track-length weighting; then parallax-based keyframe policy and speed (48-70 ms/frame in Python; C++ port plan).

change: Night front-end round. Measured: on day frames the 300th-best corner is 50-110x above the detector's noise floor (median min-eigenvalue response), at night only 3-4x -> the 300-feature budget was filled with sensor noise (2x landmark churn). Noise-adaptive detector gate (response >= 4x floor, min 60 features): night 17.4 -> 16.2, day unchanged, transition 13.4 -> 14.5 (kept: prevents noise saturation in dark scenes). Rejected after measurement: gate 8x (21.0, too few features), px_sigma 3 at night (19.4), CLAHE/blur (no gain), motion-adaptive keyframes 5 deg/15 px (night 15.5 but day 8.8 -> 12.5 at 2x cost; kept as an option, off). Two-process runs trip the 97 C thermal guard: one run at a time.
next: Night residual is track accuracy under noise, not track count: next a learned low-light enhancer (trainer exists) or per-feature uncertainty; in parallel bring up a real 3-6 camera benchmark (Hilti-Oxford 2022, 5 cams) and plan the C++ port for Jetson (48-70 ms/frame in Python now).

change: Hilti round 2. IMU model from the dataset's own 89-min static recording (Allan deviation: gyro 1.75e-4, accel 9.5e-4, walks 5e-6 / 2e-4) with the accelerometer scale factor it reveals (|a| at rest 9.641 vs g 9.812: -1.7 %, corrected via accel_scale): podslam stereo 21.1 -> 13.1 cm SE3; x2 inflation of the measured noise hurts (17.6) - inflation is IMU-specific, TUM-VI's BMI160 needed it, the BMI085 does not. Roll/pitch anchor of the first pose loosened to 0.05 rad (gravity carries the accel bias; observable): Sim3 8.9 -> 5.5, max error 49 -> 33 cm. All five cameras: 15.4 cm SE3 / 4.8 cm Sim3 (max 26) at 69 ms/frame; OpenVINS 5-cam 7.6 / 6.6 (stereo 5.4 / 3.9). KB4 lens model verified identical to OpenCV fisheye (0.0000 px) for these coefficients. Remaining gap = a -1.8 % scale (est/gt) that survives calibration, lens-model and stereo-init checks.
next: Find the visual scale bias on Hilti (per-axis accel scale, temporal-KLT sub-pixel bias, time-offset sign test), online extrinsic/time-offset refinement, then Hilti exp18 (second dense-GT sequence) and the C++/Jetson port plan.

change: Track-churn round: measured why the median landmark lives one keyframe (600-frame instrumentation): 56 % of temporal track deaths are the 1 px forward/backward check, 27 % LK status, mostly age<=3.
